land.text: Kāśī, 'conquered for good by Kosala under the latter's king Kaṃsa'; infobox 'Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE'

successors.note: The infobox lists Kosala as the successor state. Kosala then holds the land until Magadha takes Kosala (5th century BCE).

capitals.name: Vārāṇasī (Varanasi)
capitals.note: 'The capital of Kāśī was the city of' Vārāṇasī, which 'was twelve leagues in size'.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but for -600 only: Kāśī is 'Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE' (infobox); the land passes to janapada-of-kosala

keyframe_review.note: Land right, years wrong. The 5,040 km2 disc (centroid 82.82E 25.49N, 25 km north-west of Varanasi) is a Varanasi core; the page gives no area in km2 ('The Kāśī kingdom covered an area of 300 leagues' is a length) and bounds the kingdom by the Sarpikā/Syandikā river in the north and the Son in the south and east, which the disc does not reach. Cliopatria keeps Kāśī alive to -451, but the infobox has 'Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE' and the text 'finally conquered for good by Kosala under the latter's king Kaṃsa, shortly before the time of the' Buddha. The shape therefore holds for -600 only; from -599 the ground is Kosala's (see the Kosala dossier). The Mahajanapadas page's 'during Buddha's time' would put the conquest later in the 6th or 5th century, so this verdict rests on the infobox year alone (confidence 2).

correction.text: the same ground, not as a state: it belongs to janapada-of-kosala (Awadh and Kāśī) to -451, then to Magadha

keyframe_review.note: Repeats the -600 disc for -480..-451 as an independent state. By the page Kāśī was already Kosala's (it lists Mahākosala as ruling Kosala when Kāśī was already part of it, and Pasenadi controlled the Kāśī village that was Bimbisara's dowry) and 'later became a part of the empire of Magadha when Ajātasattu defeated Pasenadi's own usurper son, Viḍūḍabha, and annexed Kosala'. The ground is drawn as part of Kosala (janapada-of-kosala, to -451), not as a state of its own.

region.text: Kāśī around Vārāṇasī: 'The capital of Kāśī was the city of' Vārāṇasī; northern border 'the Sarpikā or Syandikā river', the Son 'its southern and eastern boundaries'

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Kāśī, capital Vārāṇasī, stands on the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas. The page's infobox has 'Established: c. 1375 BCE' and 'By the later Iron Age, the kingdom of Kāśī had become one of the most powerful states of Iron Age South Asia'; -600 is Cliopatria's start of the Mahajanapadas, so the date is a bridge and the earlier life is not drawn.

region.text: Kāśī around Vārāṇasī: 'The capital of Kāśī was the city of' Vārāṇasī; northern border 'the Sarpikā or Syandikā river', the Son 'its southern and eastern boundaries'

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Kosala's king Kaṃsa conquers Kāśī for good. Infobox 'Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE' and 'Kāśī was finally conquered for good by Kosala under the latter's king Kaṃsa, shortly before the time of the' Buddha. The Mahajanapadas page has 'Kashi was later incorporated into Kosala by King Kansa during Buddha's time' and the Kosala page 'annexed the powerful kingdom of Kashi' in the 6th century BCE, so the year could be later in the 6th or 5th century; Cliopatria keeps Kāśī to -451.

wars.name: Kosala's conquest of Kāśī under Kaṃsa

zones.text: Kāśī around Vārāṇasī: 'The capital of Kāśī was the city of' Vārāṇasī; northern border 'the Sarpikā or Syandikā river', the Son 'its southern and eastern boundaries'

wars.outcome: Kosala annexes Kāśī: 'Kāśī was finally conquered for good by Kosala under the latter's king Kaṃsa'; Kaṃsa is nicknamed Barānasiggaho.
wars.note: Undated except for the infobox's c. 600 BCE. Earlier back-and-forth is told without dates: a Kāśī king and his army fought Kosala to the north and seized its capital Srāvastī (Brahācatta Jātaka), and the Kosala kings Vanka and Dabbasena won suzerainty over Kāśī (Ghata and Ekarāja Jātakas). Both are before this dossier's window.

certainty.note: Only rivers bound the kingdom (Sarpikā in the north, Son in the south and east); no survey line exists.

notes: Cliopatria's Janapada of Kāśī (-600..-451, two identical 5,040 km2 discs) is cut to -600 on the strength of the Kāśī page's infobox ('Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE'); the dossier is therefore a one-year state at the map's horizon, its later life belonging to the Kosala dossier. This is the largest change in the batch and rests on one infobox figure against looser sentences ('shortly before the time of the' Buddha; 'during Buddha's time'; Kosala page '6th century BCE' and 'by the 5th century BCE'): a reviewer who prefers Cliopatria's years can restore the disc to the Kosala conquest's latest plausible date without touching the land. The infobox 'Established c. 1375 BCE' is not drawn (the Vedic Kāśī is for the additions batch sa-01-x). The Kāśī village that Bimbisara received as dowry and Pasenadi revoked (undated, Kosala dossier's war) is one village, not a cell. Magadha's absorption of Kāśī with Kosala is carried in the Kosala dossier. Pages: Kāśī and the shared Mahajanapadas page. Gazetteer: Varanasi and the Cliopatria shape exist.
